title: Accounts you'll need
content:
Professional web developers live in a handful of free services. Make these accounts now so nothing stops you later. Use the same email and, where you can, sign in with GitHub so everything connects.

  • Read and watch: about 10 minutes
  • Do: about 45 minutes
  • You make: five accounts, connected
  • You need: an email address you'll keep (a school address can expire when you graduate)
  • Support level: full

Read

Your GitHub profile is your portfolio. Employers read it. Pick a username you'd put on a resume, add a photo or avatar, and fill in your name.

Do

Sign up at github.com/signup. Personalize your profile. If you're a student, apply for the GitHub Student Developer Pack: it includes Copilot and other free tools.

Sign up at codepen.io using Sign up with GitHub. You'll build your first two cards here.

Sign up at vercel.com/signup with Continue with GitHub and choose the free Hobby plan. If anything about verification gets stuck, contact Vercel support now: they can take a few days to answer, and you need this account in chapter 4.

Make a free account at claude.ai and keep it open in a tab while you work. On a paid plan you can add Claude in Chrome to ask about the page you're looking at.

Open browser.hax.cloud once and look around. It runs HAX entirely in your browser, with no account. You'll build your capstone there.

Stuck? Ask your study buddy

Use AI to explain, not to do the work for you. Paste your own code or error with the prompt, read the answer, then close the chat and type the fix yourself. If you can't explain the fix out loud, you don't own it yet.

You're done when

Journal it

Add a heading for this page to your dev journal (the public Gist you made in Start here) and answer in Markdown:

  • Paste your GitHub profile link.
  • Which username did you choose and why?
